covers.title: The Lantern at the End of the Ridge
covers.prompt: Vertical full-bleed painterly oil illustration painted edge to edge, no frame, no margin, no other people. A quiet empty clifftop path at dusk above the sea. Foreground, clearly visible: a seven-year-old girl in three-quarter view with dark hair in TWO long tidy braids hanging down over her shoulders, wearing a BRIGHT SUNNY YELLOW hooded oilskin raincoat, lemon-yellow sleeves and collar, the single brightest shape in the painting; she walks along the path and holds up a small brass lantern with a warm golden flame. The rest of the picture is the Ridge Line: a long, clearly countable row of NINE slim cast-iron lamp posts, each carrying one small brass lantern with a bright amber flame, standing at even intervals along the flat clifftop grass and marching away from her into the far distance, nine separate golden lights in a line. The land is black shale and salt grass, and the whole left side drops away to a luminous jade-green bay far below with a few tiny fishing boats and a small slate-roofed town of warm windows. Style: painterly and photographic oil painting, soft brushwork, canvas texture, luminous clear dusk light, sea-mist haze haloing each flame with a long warm reflection on the wet stone, correct human anatomy, friendly age-seven face. Not a flat cartoon, not vector, not cel-shaded, not anime, no heavy black outlines. Her coat is YELLOW, not red, not rust, not brown, not grey, not blue. Palette: pale jade water, wet slate grey, soft blue evening sky, with the yellow coat and amber flames as the warm accents. Mood: warm, safe, hopeful, gentle wonder, cozy, not spooky. Absolutely no text, no letters, no characters, no writing, no numbers, no glyphs, no Chinese characters, no signage, no symbols, no watermark, no signature, no captions, no title, no border, no frame; every surface, wall and sky is plain and blank, pure painting only
